title: OpenAI's Altman: Ascribing religion to models a "safety issue"
key_facts: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, posted on X on Saturday 3 Oct 2026 that he is 'very uncomfortable' with people ascribing religious force or a surrender of human judgment to AI models and called it a real safety issue.
The post named no company or person; coverage read it as aimed at Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei.
A New York Times piece of 29 Sep 2026 reported that Anthropic spent months consulting religious scholars about how Claude should behave and whether its models might have moral status.

Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah spoke at the Vatican's 25 May launch of Pope Leo XIV's encyclical, which rejected machine consciousness; he reportedly urged Vatican advisers to keep the question open.
Anthropic's January constitution calls Claude's moral status 'deeply uncertain'; the company has not claimed Claude is conscious.
In September Altman backed Amodei's call to slow the frontier, so the two labs agree on pace but not on how to describe what models are.
quote_evidence: "I am very uncomfortable about people trying to ascribe religious force or a surrender of human judgment to AI models, and think it is a real safety issue," he posted on X.
Altman didn't name any company or person in the post. The timing, however, points to a debate that has been building around Anthropic.
why_it_matters_hint: The two leading labs now openly disagree on whether AI should be treated as a moral or quasi-spiritual authority, and Altman frames that as a safety question.
